notes: Machine-readable policy table. Loaded by src/fhir_sulo/identity.
No entry here asserts owl:sameAs between a FHIR resource and a person.
A resolved FHIR reference is lineage, not a person-equivalence claim.

entity_iri.entity_kind_segments_note: Authoritative map from a permitted entity kind to its IRI segment. person_segment above is kept as the compatibility alias for person and MUST agree with this map; a contract test asserts it.
entity_iri.permitted_entity_kinds_rule: OntoClean (DR-010). entity_kind is one of key_input_fields, so it is an IDENTITY CRITERION, and an identity criterion must come from a RIGID property -- one that holds necessarily of its instances. 'practitioner' and 'patient' are ANTI-RIGID: a person can stop being either without ceasing to exist. They are roles, carried by a Role individual attached to the person, never by the person's entity kind or IRI.
entity_iri.undeclared_entity_kind_note: Was NOT rejected before 2026-10-03: the service slugified any kind it was handed into an IRI segment, which is how entity_kind='practitioner' produced practitioner-<hash> without ever being declared here. Rejecting closes that path; adding a kind is now a reviewed edit to entity_kind_segments and needs a rigidity argument.

key_style_options.scoped-hash: person-<32 lowercase hex chars>. Source-scoped by construction; two sources that both hold Patient/p123 get different IRIs. Safe default.
key_style_options.legacy-concept-note: person-<resource-id-slug>, matching the concept note's ex:person-p123. ONLY valid when entity_iri.single_source_scope is set; a request from any other scope is rejected, not silently keyed.

entity_iri.key_revision_note: Deliberately NOT the table's semantic version. Entity IRIs are stable across every policy edit that does not change the keying answer; bumping this revision is an explicit, breaking re-keying decision that needs a DR-4xx record. Agent 6 can therefore treat an entity IRI as stable while identity-policy.version moves.
entity_iri.key_input_normalisation: Unicode NFC, then canonical JSON (sorted keys, no whitespace, ASCII-escaped), then sha256. No timestamps, no process state, no Python hash().

key_style_decision.history: DR-005 decided scoped-slug on 2026-09-29 for reviewability and it was never applied -- the policy shipped scoped-hash and no test asserted the live value against the record. Found by Agent 5 during IR-602. Applying it on 2026-10-03 surfaced the reason the decision was wrong, and it was reverted the same day.
key_style_decision.why_scoped_hash_wins: scoped-slug embeds the FHIR resource id in the SEMANTIC individual's IRI: person-synthea-pilot-r4-p123-144658ab. No owl:sameAs is asserted and the two IRIs are distinct, so it does not breach concept note section 2 literally. But it names the person after the record, which invites exactly the conflation section 2 exists to prevent -- a reader seeing 'p123' in a person IRI will treat it as Patient/p123. Opacity is the cheaper guarantee, and the reviewer signed off R7 ('the FHIR resource and its interpretation are distinct individuals') against the opaque form.
key_style_decision.cost_accepted: Expected graphs carry 32-hex IRIs and are harder for a human to read. That was DR-005's argument for the slug; it is real but it is the lesser concern, and R7 was reviewed successfully in this form.
key_style_decision.guard: tests/contracts/identity/test_key_style_matches_the_record.py asserts the live key_style equals the recorded decision, which is the fix for the drift that let this sit unnoticed for four days.

reference_scope.rationale: Concept note section 2 and plan section 7: never merge two references into one person without recorded evidence.

accepted_merge_evidence.when: A reference carries exactly one FHIR Identifier whose system is listed in person_identifying_identifier_systems.
accepted_merge_evidence.then: The person is keyed on (key_scheme, key_revision, entity_kind, identifier_system, identifier_value) and NOT on source scope or resource address.
accepted_merge_evidence.why_this_is_keying_and_not_merging: A business identifier in an agreed namespace IS an identity criterion for the person -- that is what Identifier.system means. Keying on it directly gives one IRI, deterministically, with no post-hoc graph rewriting, no owl:sameAs between records, and no reasoning needed to collapse two nodes. A Patient reference and a Practitioner reference carrying the same national number arrive at the same IRI because they are the same person, not because a merge pass fused them.
accepted_merge_evidence.deliberately_not_source_scoped: This is the recorded evidence that reference_scope.cross_source_merge requires. A national identifier is global by construction; scoping it per source would defeat the only thing it is for.
accepted_merge_evidence.cost_accepted: An entity keyed on an identifier has a DIFFERENT IRI from the same person keyed on a record address. If a record later starts carrying an allowlisted identifier, that person's IRI moves. That is a re-keying event, visible and deterministic, not a silent drift -- but it is real, and it is why the allowlist is a reviewed list rather than 'any identifier'.

reference_scope.accepted_merge_evidence_note: No longer empty. R8b was answered on 2026-10-03: a shared person-identifying business identifier merges. The ALLOWLIST below is still empty, so no merge can occur yet; adding a system to it is the reviewed decision, and is what switches this on.

contained_reference_scoping.rationale: A FHIR contained resource has no existence outside the resource that contains it. Two Observations that each carry a contained Patient '#p-inline' describe two different people, and keying them on the dataset scope alone would merge them.
contained_reference_scoping.strip_leading_hash_note: '#p-inline' and 'p-inline' name the same contained resource; normalising here keeps one entity rather than two.
contained_reference_scoping.missing_container_url_note: A contained reference whose container is unknown cannot be scoped. Rejecting is the conservative outcome: silently falling back to the dataset scope is precisely the merge this rule prevents.
contained_reference_scoping.owner_note: IR-604. This rule used to be applied by each caller - src/fhir_sulo/pipeline/services.py baked it into SourceScope.scope_id, and src/fhir_sulo/ingest/identity_port.py's MockIdentityService had a second, incompatible formula. It is identity policy, so it is declared here and applied by the identity service.

resolution_rules.when: Exactly one candidate whose resolved_resource_type is in the request's expected_resource_types.
Zero candidates supplied by reference resolution.
More than one candidate and they do not all agree on (source_scope_id, resource_type, resource_id).
More than one candidate and all agree on (source_scope_id, resource_type, resource_id).
resolution_rules.note: Not a merge across identities: it is the same triple of key inputs observed more than once.

resolution_rules.when: A candidate's resource_type is not in expected_resource_types.
A required key input field is absent or empty after normalisation.
A candidate's kind is 'contained' and it carries a container_url.
resolution_rules.note: Keyed in scope '{scope_id}|contained|{container_url}', so '#p-inline' in two containers is two entities. See contained_reference_scoping.

resolution_rules.when: A candidate's kind is 'contained' and it carries no container_url.
key_style is legacy-concept-note and the candidate's source_scope_id differs from entity_iri.single_source_scope.
resolution_rules.note: Guards the readable key style against the exact failure it invites.

resolution_rules.when: The request's entity_kind is not a key of entity_iri.entity_kind_segments.
resolution_rules.note: DR-010. entity_kind is a key input, so it is an identity criterion and must name a rigid property. Anti-rigid terms ('practitioner', 'patient') are roles and belong on a Role individual attached to the person.
Deliberately NOT ID-R10. This is a defect in THIS FILE, not in the caller's entity_kind, and recording it as ID-R10 would blame the request in the audit trail for a policy that contradicts itself.

resolution_rules.when: Exactly one allowlisted person-identifying identifier is present.
resolution_rules.note: Keyed on the identifier, not source-scoped. See accepted_merge_evidence.

resolution_rules.when: More than one allowlisted person-identifying identifier is present and they do not all agree on (system, value).
resolution_rules.note: Deterministic keying cannot choose between them, and picking the first would make identity depend on element order. Resolving this properly needs transitive entity resolution across identifiers, which is stateful, is not a keying rule, and is not in scope for this pilot.

resolution_rules.when: A candidate carries a business identifier, has no resource address, and no carried system is in person_identifying_identifier_systems.
resolution_rules.note: Distinct from ID-R6 incomplete-key-inputs, which is true of this case but says nothing useful. This names the actual reason and the actual remedy.

ambiguity.api_contract: Rejection is a distinct return type with no entity IRI attribute. There is no Optional-IRI return anywhere in the identity API.

quality_identity.mode_status: SET (provisional) - reviewer answered R2 = B on 2026-09-30. Explicitly not settled; see reviewer_decision.revisit.
quality_identity.key_revision_note: As for entity_iri.key_revision: quality IRIs are stable across policy edits that do not change the keying answer. Note that CHANGING quality_identity.mode does change every quality IRI, unavoidably, because the two modes key on different inputs. That is a graph-key-affecting decision, not an incidental version bump.
quality_identity.unset_behaviour_note: While mode is null every quality-identity request returns a rejection with reason_code quality-identity-policy-unset. Nothing downstream can accidentally ship a guessed policy.

persistent-per-person-code.description: One persisting quality entity per (person, observable code). The same renal-filtration quality IRI is reused across every eGFR observation for that person.
persistent-per-person-code.implication: Independent records about the same person and code converge on one quality node. Matches the concept note's ex:renal-quality-p123 example graph.
persistent-per-person-code.risk: Two records the project does not actually intend to be about one persisting quality will merge.

per-observation.description: A quality entity keyed by person, observable code, the source observation version, and the clinically relevant time.
per-observation.implication: Independent records never merge unknowingly (concept note section 4).
per-observation.risk: A query for 'the patient's renal filtration quality' returns many distinct nodes; cross-observation trend queries must join on the code rather than on the quality IRI.

quality_identity.reviewer_question: Does a quality IRI persist across observations for a patient (persistent-per-person-code), or is it keyed per observation plus time plus code (per-observation)? Concept note section 4 and plan Gate 0 both flag this as a reviewer decision. Both behaviours are implemented; the default is deliberately unset and rejects.

reviewer_decision.status: provisional - the underlying question is NOT resolved
reviewer_decision.reviewer_words: Whether there is a single quality of a particular kind for an individual, or whether there can be multiple distinct instances, is not yet resolved. One per event with its associated value is probably safest. This needs revisiting in a coherent theory, compared against other upper-level ontologies.
reviewer_decision.consequence_measured: Under per-observation a correction (v1 to v2) mints a NEW quality node while the quantity keeps its IRI, so a correction is visible in the graph's identity. Under persistent-per-person-code it would not be.
reviewer_decision.revisit: Reconcile quality individuation against other ULOs before clinical use. Both modes remain implemented and tested; switching re-keys every quality IRI and is a graph migration, not a configuration change.

person_identifying_identifier_systems_no: Identifier.system URIs that identify a PERSON, such as a national person number or a national provider number. EMPTY BY DESIGN and not populated by the implementation: which namespaces identify a person is a clinical/governance decision, not an engineering one. While it is empty the mechanism is fully implemented and tested but can never fire, so behaviour is identical to before R8b was answered. A local MRN does NOT belong here: it identifies a patient record at one organisation, not a human.
